Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle can be understood by comparing it to taking a photograph of a fast-moving car. If you use a very fast shutter speed to capture the car's exact position clearly, the image becomes sharp, but you lose information about how fast it was moving because the motion is frozen. Conversely, if you use a slow shutter speed to capture the blur of motion (momentum), the car's exact location becomes smeared and uncertain. This trade-off between knowing position and momentum precisely is fundamental to quantum mechanics.

The name of the planet humans live on is Earth.
